newsitem.title: USA: INSTANT VIEW - U.S. stocks seen up after jobs data.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - U.S. stocks seen up after jobs data.

text.p: U.S. stocks were are seen opening higher on Friday after a report on January U.S. employment, analysts said.
PHIL ORLANDO, CHIEF INVESTMENT OFFICER OF VALUE LINE'S ASSET MANAGEMENT DIVISION

-- "The actual number at 271,000 was more than we expected. On the surface it's a strong number, bad for bonds... Importantly, the average hourly wage component was smaller than expected, implying benign inflation continues."
-- "The market was clearly focusing on the inflation aspect rather than nominal non-farm jobs."
The Labor Department reported the U.S. economy added 271,000 new jobs in January compared to a revised rise of 261,000 in December.
Wall Street had expected the report to show non-farm payrolls expanding by 237,000 jobs in January, according to a Reuters poll.
Average weekly hours declined to 34.1 hours from 34.8 in December.
RICHARD CRIPPS CHIEF MARKET STRATEGIST AT LEGG MASON WOOD WALKER:
-- "The number was higher as it pertains to the actual non-farm payrolls. The positive is clearly the hourly earnings, which showed a decline. That's the clear positive."
-- "The market was fairly flat in terms of its positioning for it and that's why we're seeing a strong rise."
LARRY WACHTEL, ANALYST AT PRUDENTIAL SECURITIES:
"Hourly earnings were much less than expected and the unemployment rate rose. It is fairly benign and the rally in bonds is a sigh of relief that the data were not worse."
